name: Ironbloom — Chrome Pride Street Movement
description: Ironbloom began in the Tier 2 fabrication districts of the old South Loop as a defiant response to corporate augmentation advertising that portrayed chrome as aspirational only when clean, hidden, and expensive. Members celebrate visible, imperfect, and self-installed augmentation — exposed wiring, mismatched plating, aug work done in kitchen clinics rather than licensed suites. Their signature aesthetic is 'bloom scarring': the deliberate oxidation of chrome in floral or botanical patterns using acid baths and heat. Weekly gatherings called Showings happen under the Wacker Overpass, where members display new work and rank each other's ingenuity over unlicensed Tier 2 food stalls.
cultural_impact: Ironbloom has created a black market for aug customization that undercuts licensed corporate clinics, pressuring NovaBodi Corp to launch a cheaper 'raw aesthetic' product line widely mocked as corporate cosplay. Their bloom-scarring technique has spread to Tier 3, where it is worn ironically by people who can afford better.
story_hooks: A Tier 4 corporate heir gets bloom-scarring done secretly and is photographed — their corponation parent demands the artist found and the work reversed before a major IPO.
A young Ironbloom member's self-installed aug is failing, and the only person who can fix it without corporate records is the original underground fabricator who has gone missing.
Ironbloom's weekly Showing is about to be raided — someone sold the location, and the community needs to determine who the informant is before next week's event.
